Laurence Gonzales Photo: Ben Gonzales
Laurence Gonzales is the son of a Mexican biophysicist and an Irish-German woman with a flair for poetry. His first poem was published in Poetry Magazine in 1970, followed by short stories and other poems published in the literary magazines of the time. His career took off when he switched from poetry and fiction to nonfiction. As early as 1973, he had decided to bring together the worlds of science and poetry to create a new kind of nonfiction.

...

rs of research and experimentation, he brought those elements together in Deep Survival: Who Lives, Who Dies, and Why . That book created a genre, much imitated, and has remained a consistent best seller since its publication in 2003.

...

Another achievement in his pursuit of this new approach to factual writing was Flight 232: A Story of Disaster and Survival . The first complete reconstruction of the fatal crash of a modern airliner, it was called "A kind of miracle" by Michael Korda and "a new masterpiece" by Richard Rhodes. It represented a landmark in journalism, penetrating an unseen and deadly realm of our daily lives, never before revealed, to demonstrate the beating heart of human compassion within. His most recent novel is Lucy. His most recent nonfiction book is Isolato: An Intimate Portrait of Cormac McCarthy

Flight 232
In FLIGHT 232: A Story of Disaster and Survival , Laurence Gonzales re-creates, minute by minute, the harrowing journey, not only of those inside the doomed plane but also those who had to meet it on the ground and those who had to treat the wounded, attend the dead, and pick up the many pieces. Through exhaustive research and extensive interviews with everyone from air traffic controllers to rescue workers, survivors to the pilots themselves, Gonzales crafts a riveting tale of heroism and triumph in the face of death.
